recommendations.headline: Only 18% of 2,729 calls convert to an order even though 55% end in a 'callback' holding pattern - the gap is driven by follow-up and clarity failures, not price, since satisfied calls close at 71% vs just 10% for neutral calls.
behaviour: Price shopping dominates: 545 calls tagged price_shopper and 320 comparing_quotes, yet price is explicitly discussed in only 32% of calls (price_reaction not_discussed=1858/2729) - most 'price_high' objections (467) still convert at 23% when actually engaged.
Deals stall rather than die: 1,502 calls (55%) end in callback vs only 493 (18%) orders and 117 (4%) not_interested - the pipeline is full of warm but unclosed leads.
Stock availability is the #1 stated need (502 calls) and 2nd most common objection (441), but calls with this objection win only 16% of the time, pointing to real fulfilment gaps.

Segment handling is uneven: fabricators convert at 36% and dealers at 31%, but the 683 'unknown segment' calls (25% of volume) convert at only 15%, suggesting reps often don't capture who they're talking to.
Credit/LC demand is real but poorly served: 124 credit_terms objections and 140 needs_credit tags, yet this objection has the lowest win rate (12%) of any category.
satisfaction: Satisfaction is the strongest predictor of winning: satisfied calls (798, 29%) win 71% of the time vs 10% for neutral calls (1,518, 56%) and 3% for dissatisfied (273, 10%) - lifting a call from neutral to satisfied matters more than any discount.

Negative sentiment appears in 479 calls (17.5%) and dissatisfaction in 273 calls (10%), closely tracking rep-side issues: no_follow_up_fixed (506), slow_or_unclear_answer (462) and no_quote_sent (290).

Price is rarely the dealbreaker it seems: 'too_high' is the final reaction in only 104 calls (4%) while 'negotiating' (541, 20%) and 'accepted' (226, 8%) show most price conversations do move toward a deal once engaged.

conversion.title: Close the follow-up loop
conversion.evidence: 506 calls (18.5%) show no_follow_up_fixed and 1,502 calls (55%) end as 'callback'; multiple customer questions are literally 'why didn't you call back'.
conversion.action: Require every call to end with a specific date/time commitment logged in CRM; managers audit open callbacks daily and escalate any over 48 hours.

conversion.title: Speed up and standardise quoting
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent in 290 calls and slow_or_unclear_answer in 462 calls; many customer questions ask 'where is my quote.'
conversion.action: Set a same-day SLA for sending written quotes via WhatsApp/email and track quote-sent rate per rep weekly.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order flagged in 200 calls while order_pct is only 18%.
conversion.action: Train reps to explicitly request PO confirmation whenever price is accepted or being negotiated (541 negotiating + 226 accepted calls).

conversion.title: Fix stock-visibility and offer alternatives
conversion.evidence: stock_availability is the top customer need (502) and 2nd top objection (441, win rate 16%); didnt_offer_alternative flagged 206 times.
conversion.action: Give reps a live stock dashboard and mandate offering an alternate size/brand/origin whenever the requested item is unavailable.

conversion.title: Create a clear credit/LC decision path
conversion.evidence: credit_terms has the lowest win rate (12%) of all objections; needs_credit (140) and credit_period need (110); several deals lost explicitly 'because we could not offer credit terms'.
conversion.action: Define an internal credit/LC eligibility slab for vetted dealers/bulk buyers and commit to a fixed turnaround time for manager approval.

conversion.title: Capture segment and requirement early
conversion.evidence: Unknown-segment calls (683, 25% of volume) convert at 15% vs 31-36% for known segments; didnt_ask_requirement flagged in 66 calls.
conversion.action: Make segment and requirement capture mandatory in the first minute of every call for accurate follow-up routing.

conversion.title: Coach for clarity and value, not discounting
conversion.evidence: Satisfied calls win 71% vs 10% for neutral; didnt_highlight_value flagged in 108 calls; slow_or_unclear_answer in 462 calls.
conversion.action: Review recorded calls with unclear answers monthly and coach reps to lead with certainty, specifics and value points before any price talk.

offers.why: cutting_processing need flagged in 270 calls; recurring questions on custom cut lengths and rates.

offers.why: min_quantity objection in 62 calls and small_quantity need in 40 calls limit entry for smaller buyers.

loyalty.how: Call customers after dispatch to confirm weight, grade and quality before disputes arise
loyalty.why: after_sales_support need (35) plus recurring weight-shortage and quality complaints in call summaries.

non_price_benefits.why: quality_doubt objection in 194 calls and test_certificate need in 176 calls.

non_price_benefits.why: fast_delivery need (461) and site_delivery need (132), plus urgent_buyer tagged 268 times.

non_price_benefits.title: Proactive rate and stock communication

top_questions.question: Can you reduce the price / give a discount?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the ask, reframe around quality, certification and delivery reliability, and offer to check volume-based terms with a manager rather than quoting a number on the spot.

top_questions.question: Can we get material on LC or credit terms?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain standard payment terms clearly, note that larger or repeat orders can be escalated for manager review, and give a specific timeline for a decision.

top_questions.question: What is today's/current rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Share the current rate promptly via WhatsApp/call, mention any market trend, and invite the customer to lock in before a possible change.

top_questions.question: Is the stock/size available now?
top_questions.answer_tip: Check live stock before answering; if unavailable, immediately offer the nearest alternate size, brand or plant origin.

top_questions.question: Why hasn't my quote or follow-up happened?
top_questions.answer_tip: Apologise, give a firm callback time, log it in CRM, and loop in a supervisor if this is a repeat issue for that customer.

top_questions.question: Can you provide a test certificate / MTC?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm TC/MTC is provided with dispatch as standard and offer to share a sample certificate in advance if needed for approvals.

top_questions.question: Can you cut to a custom size or length?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm cutting/processing capability, ask for exact specification, and mention standard size options available to compare.

top_questions.question: Will you deliver to site and what about transport cost?
top_questions.answer_tip: Clarify ex-work vs door-delivery options and explain transport cost calculation transparently based on distance and load.

recommendations.headline: Varsha leaves 69% of calls (1625/2344) without even discussing price and fails to lock a concrete follow-up in 443 calls (19%) - these two gaps, not price, are why only 18% of calls convert to an order while 55% stall as 'callback'.
behaviour: Price-shopping dominates: 'price_shopper' is the top tagged behaviour (433 calls) and 254 calls show 'comparing_quotes', with price_high (389 calls) and competitor_cheaper (83 calls, only 8% win) as top objections.

Most customers actually need service, not discount: stock_availability (426), fast_delivery (409), regular_updates (300) and cutting_processing (262) are the top stated needs - far ahead of credit_period (88).
A large share are already engaged buyers: repeat_buyer (219), bulk_buyer (244) and urgent_buyer (240) behaviours are common, so retention/service matters as much as new acquisition.
Dealers are 51% of all calls (1191) but convert at only 31%, while fabricators (328 calls) convert highest at 36% - segment handling is uneven.
Credit-seeking and indecisive customers are a meaningful chunk (needs_credit 120, indecisive 119) and credit_terms objection converts worst among financial objections (11% win on 103 calls).
satisfaction: Call satisfaction is middling: only 669/2344 calls (29%) end 'satisfied', 57% are neutral and 247 (11%) are dissatisfied - and win-rate collapses from 72% when satisfied to just 10% (neutral) and 3% (dissatisfied), showing satisfaction is the single strongest predictor of a sale.

Price is rarely even discussed - 1625 calls (69%) show 'not_discussed' in price_reaction - yet price_high is still flagged as an objection in 389 calls, suggesting the issue is clarity/confidence on calls, not the actual price level.
When price is discussed, most customers negotiate rather than reject: 443 'negotiating' vs only 91 'too_high' - price resistance is often workable, not a hard no.

Rep-side gaps directly track the dissatisfaction: no_follow_up_fixed (443) and slow_or_unclear_answer (409) are the two most common missed actions, matching the 57% of calls that stay merely 'neutral'.

conversion.title: Always lock a specific follow-up before ending the call
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed is the #1 miss (443 calls, 19%) and 1298 calls (55%) end as vague 'callback' rather than a decision.
conversion.action: Never close a call with 'I'll check and call back' - state an exact date/time/channel (e.g. 'I will WhatsApp the quote by 5pm today') and log it for a mandatory callback.

conversion.title: Give faster, clearer answers on calls
conversion.evidence: slow_or_unclear_answer is the #2 miss (409 calls, 17%), and price_enquiry is the top intent (716 calls, 31%).
conversion.action: Keep a quick-reference rate/stock/spec sheet for top products (plate, channel, TMT, angle, HR coil) open during calls to avoid stalling or vague replies.

conversion.title: Send the quotation during or right after the call
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent happened in 260 calls (11%); multiple lost-call summaries show deals lost purely because the quote was delayed.
conversion.action: Send a WhatsApp/email quote within the call wherever possible, or within a committed timeframe (e.g. same day) - and confirm receipt.

conversion.title: Offer an alternative whenever stock is short
conversion.evidence: didnt_offer_alternative missed in 183 calls; stock_availability is the 2nd biggest objection (384 calls) with only 17% win.
conversion.action: When an item/size is unavailable, immediately suggest the nearest available size, brand or cut option before ending the call instead of just noting it's out of stock.

conversion.title: Explicitly ask for the order
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order missed in 152 calls; only 431 of 2344 calls (18%) close as an order versus 208 marked merely 'interested'.
conversion.action: After every quote/spec confirmation, ask a direct closing question ('Shall I book this quantity for you today?').

conversion.title: Lead with value before price
conversion.evidence: didnt_highlight_value missed in 90 calls; competitor_cheaper objection wins only 8% (83 calls) and price_high only 21% (389 calls).
conversion.action: Mention certification, cutting service, delivery speed and stock reliability before quoting a rate, so price is judged against value, not in isolation.

conversion.title: Proactively confirm requirement and price position early
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_requirement missed in 55 calls; 1625 calls (69%) never reach a price discussion at all.
conversion.action: Start every price-enquiry call by confirming exact spec/quantity/timeline, then move the conversation to price within the same call rather than leaving it open.

offers.title: Cut-to-size / processing as a standard add-on
offers.for_whom: Fabricators and customers needing custom lengths
offers.why: cutting_processing is the 4th highest need (262 calls) and repeat questions ask for custom cutting, 5m lengths, and specific widths.

offers.title: Fast-track delivery slot for urgent orders
offers.why: fast_delivery is the 2nd top need (409 calls) and urgent_buyer behaviour appears in 240 calls; several won calls cite next-day/night delivery as the clincher.

offers.title: WhatsApp stock & price update subscription
offers.why: regular_updates need (300 calls) and comparing_quotes behaviour (254 calls) show customers want fresher info without having to call repeatedly.

offers.title: Bundled documentation package (MTC/Test Certificate issued by default)
offers.why: test_certificate need (162 calls) and quality_doubt objection (176 calls, 20% win) are frequent; many questions ask specifically for MTC/TC.

offers.title: Small-lot / split-quantity option
offers.why: min_quantity objection (58 calls) and real examples show deals lost when minimum supply (5-6 tons) didn't match customer's need (e.g. 2-ton coil).

offers.title: Consider a structured credit/payment term option for vetted repeat dealers
offers.why: needs_credit (120 calls) and credit_terms objection has the lowest win rate among financial objections (11%, 103 calls); one lost-deal summary explicitly cites lack of credit terms as the reason for losing the customer.

loyalty.title: Reserved-stock priority for repeat buyers
loyalty.how: Flag repeat_buyer accounts in the system and hold/reserve cut stock for their recurring order pattern.
loyalty.why: repeat_buyer behaviour is common (219 calls) and one won-call example shows a customer explicitly asking that reserved cut coil be kept only for him.

loyalty.title: Dedicated proactive update calls instead of waiting for customer to chase
loyalty.how: Schedule a short status call/WhatsApp update for open quotes and pending POs at fixed intervals.
loyalty.why: no_follow_up_fixed is the top miss (443 calls) and many unconverted summaries show frustration from customers chasing unanswered quotes.

loyalty.title: Same-day certificate/documentation turnaround for loyal accounts
loyalty.how: Pre-prepare MTC/TC templates for repeat product-grade combinations so they can be issued faster.
loyalty.why: test_certificate need (162 calls) and quality_assurance (227 calls) are recurring asks, especially from repeat industrial/fabricator customers.

loyalty.title: Recognise and reward referrals
loyalty.how: Track referral-sourced calls and acknowledge/thank referring customers (e.g. priority handling on their next order).
loyalty.why: referral behaviour is low (15 calls) and loyal_to_us only 12 - a visible recognition programme could grow this small but valuable segment.

loyalty.title: Segment-specific account care for lower-converting groups
loyalty.how: Assign consistent single-point contact and more frequent technical check-ins for industrial and contractor segments.
loyalty.why: industrial (26% win) and contractor (29% win) convert below dealer/fabricator averages, despite steady call volume (117 and 70 calls respectively).

non_price_benefits.title: Quality assurance & certification
non_price_benefits.why: quality_doubt objection seen in 176 calls (20% win) and test_certificate is a top-10 need (162 calls); many questions ask for MTC/grade confirmation.

non_price_benefits.title: Cutting & processing capability
non_price_benefits.why: cutting_processing is the 4th highest need (262 calls) with repeated custom-size requests in call summaries and questions.

non_price_benefits.title: Reliable, fast delivery including site delivery
non_price_benefits.why: fast_delivery (409 calls) and site_delivery (117 calls) are top needs; multiple won calls closed because urgent/next-day delivery was promised.

non_price_benefits.title: Stock availability and consistent supply
non_price_benefits.why: stock_availability is the top customer need (426 calls) and also the 2nd most common objection (384 calls, only 17% win) - reassurance here is high-value.

non_price_benefits.title: Technical/spec advice
non_price_benefits.why: needs_technical_help is the 2nd most common behaviour (314 calls) and technical_advice is a top need (183 calls) - grade/size clarity (E250 vs E350, per-meter vs per-ton) recurs often.

non_price_benefits.title: Transparent paperwork (GST, e-way bill, invoicing)
non_price_benefits.why: Multiple questions concern e-way bill issues, GST inclusion, and invoice company-name mix-ups - clear upfront documentation reduces friction and dissatisfaction.

top_questions.question: Is there scope to reduce the price / can you match a competitor's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the comparison, restate the value (certification, cutting, delivery reliability) before addressing rate, and offer to check with management rather than refusing outright.

top_questions.question: Can payment be done via LC or credit terms?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain current payment terms clearly, note the request, and commit to checking with management and following up by a fixed time.

top_questions.question: Is the item in stock / what sizes are available?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give a direct stock answer immediately; if unavailable, proactively suggest the closest available size, brand or grade.

top_questions.question: Can you send the quotation/proforma invoice quickly via WhatsApp?
top_questions.answer_tip: Send it during the call if possible, or commit to an exact time and follow through without the customer having to chase.

top_questions.question: Will you handle transport/delivery and by when?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm delivery date, transport inclusion/exclusion, and any loading charges clearly upfront to avoid later disputes.

top_questions.question: Can you provide MTC/test certificates?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm certificates are standard practice and specify exactly when they will be shared (e.g. with dispatch documents).

top_questions.question: Why hasn't my quote/order been followed up on?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the delay honestly, give a firm new follow-up time, and escalate internally if the delay is beyond the rep's control.

top_questions.question: Do you deal in [other products like pipes] or other grades (E250/E350, IS2062)?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm current product/grade range accurately; if outside current range, offer to check sourcing options and follow up rather than leaving it unanswered.

recommendations.headline: Venkatesh's win rate swings from 67% when the customer leaves satisfied to just 10% when neutral (129 vs 192 calls) - closing that satisfaction gap by fixing the three biggest rep misses (no fixed follow-up 63x, slow/unclear answers 53x, not asking for the order 48x) is the single highest-leverage fix to lift the 16% overall order rate.
behaviour: 112 of 385 callers behave as price_shoppers and 66 are actively comparing_quotes, so most calls start as benchmarking, not firm intent.
60% of calls (233/385) never even reach a price discussion (price_reaction 'not_discussed'), showing conversations stall before the real decision point.
204/385 calls (53%) end in 'callback' and 61 end 'unclear' - indecision is the default outcome, not a clear yes/no.
52 customers are bulk_buyers and 28 are repeat_buyers, but only 28 show urgent_buyer intent - most are planning ahead, not buying today.
20 customers explicitly need credit and 21 raise credit_terms as an objection (only 19% win rate on that objection), showing credit is a real but unresolved blocker.
satisfaction: Only 129/385 calls (33.5%) leave the customer satisfied; 192 (50%) are merely neutral and 26 (6.8%) dissatisfied.
Satisfaction is the strongest predictor of a sale: 67% win rate when satisfied vs 10% when neutral and 0% when dissatisfied.
Price itself isn't the biggest killer - price_high objection still wins 31% of the time, while stock_availability (11%), competitor_cheaper (9%) and quality_doubt (6%) convert far worse.

Transport_cost objection actually closes 60% of the time (9/15 calls), suggesting price-related friction is often resolved once Venkatesh engages, but stock/quality doubts are not being handled as well.

conversion.title: Fix every promised follow-up
conversion.evidence: no_follow_up_fixed flagged on 63 calls - the single biggest rep miss, and 204 calls already sit in 'callback' status
conversion.action: On every call, state and log a specific day/time for the next contact, and call back exactly then - even if there is no update yet.

conversion.title: Answer rate/stock questions faster and clearer
conversion.evidence: slow_or_unclear_answer flagged on 53 calls; 'what is today's rate' and stock questions dominate the question list
conversion.action: Keep a live rate/stock sheet open during calls so Venkatesh can answer size-wise rates and availability on the spot instead of 'I'll check and revert'.

conversion.title: Always ask for the order
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_for_order flagged on 48 calls despite 46 'interested' outcomes sitting unconverted
conversion.action: End every call where the customer is engaged with a direct close - 'Shall I book this quantity today?' - instead of letting the call end on information only.

conversion.title: Send the quote immediately, in writing
conversion.evidence: no_quote_sent flagged on 30 calls; many well-run calls succeeded specifically because a PDF/WhatsApp quote was sent fast
conversion.action: Send a WhatsApp/PDF quote before hanging up or within the hour, every time a rate is discussed.

conversion.title: Offer an alternative when stock is short
conversion.evidence: didnt_offer_alternative flagged on 23 calls; stock_availability is the #2 objection (57 calls) but only wins 11% of the time
conversion.action: When the requested size/brand is unavailable, proactively suggest an alternate size, brand or part-quantity instead of ending the call.

conversion.title: Lead with value, not just rate, on quality-doubt calls
conversion.evidence: didnt_highlight_value flagged on 18 calls; quality_doubt objection only wins 6% of the time (18 calls)
conversion.action: Proactively mention test certificates, fresh stock and brand tagging before the customer has to ask, especially for Vizag/SAIL-tagged material.

conversion.title: Probe requirement before quoting
conversion.evidence: didnt_ask_requirement flagged on 11 calls; segments like dealer (227 calls, 31% win) and contractor (39 calls, 36% win) respond better when needs are clarified upfront
conversion.action: Confirm quantity, size, grade and delivery location before quoting a rate, so the first quote is already matched to the real need.

offers.title: Real-time stock availability check
offers.for_whom: all customers asking about size/brand stock

offers.title: Cutting/bending/processing service

non_price_benefits.title: Technical sizing/bending advice

non_price_benefits.title: Transparent loading/transport cost breakdown

top_questions.question: What is today's rate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Quote the current rate immediately from a live sheet and briefly note any market trend, rather than promising to check and call back.

top_questions.question: Can this be done on LC / credit terms?
top_questions.answer_tip: Explain the credit evaluation process and timeline clearly, and commit to a specific date for manager confirmation.

top_questions.question: Is [size/brand] available in stock?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm real stock status on the call; if unavailable, immediately offer an alternate size, brand or partial quantity.

top_questions.question: Why didn't you follow up / respond to my call?
top_questions.answer_tip: Acknowledge the gap, give a concrete reason, and set a firm new callback time that will be honoured.

top_questions.question: Can you match a competitor's lower price?
top_questions.answer_tip: Avoid simply matching; highlight certification, fresh stock, delivery reliability and service as the reasons for the rate.

top_questions.question: Can you send the quote via WhatsApp/PDF?
top_questions.answer_tip: Send the quote during or immediately after the call so the customer has it in writing without delay.

top_questions.question: Will you provide a test certificate?
top_questions.answer_tip: Confirm certificate availability upfront and offer to send it along with the tag details before being asked twice.

top_questions.question: Why is the transport/loading charge so high?
top_questions.answer_tip: Give an itemised breakdown of loading and transport costs so the customer sees it is justified, not arbitrary.
